description: A method's expression body reads its own instance with leading dots
code:
class Rect(this.w, this.h):
    def area() => .w * .h
r = Rect(3, 4)
assert(r.area(), 12)
r.h = 5
r.area()

description: A method's indented body reads its instance in conditions and returns
Methods read their instance in templates and call its other methods
code:
class Item(this.name, this.price, this.qty):
    def total() => .price * .qty
    def label() => `${.name}: ${.total()}`
i = Item("pen", 2, 3)
assert(i.label(), "pen: 6")
i.qty = 4
i.label()

description: A Python-style self method reads its instance with leading dots
A constructor body reads the instance it is building
Variables and destructuring declarations in a method read the instance
code:
class Pair(this.a, this.b):
    def swapped():
        first, second = [.b, .a]
        total = .a + .b
        return [first, second, total]
p = Pair(1, 2)
assert(p.swapped()[2], 3)
p.swapped()

description: A property assignment in a method reads the object of its own target
A lambda in a method takes an instance property through a local
A comprehension source and a quantifier condition read the instance
code:
class Grades(this.scores, this.minimum):
    def passed() => [s for s in .scores if s >= 50]
    def all_passed() => all s in .scores: s >= .minimum
g = Grades([40, 70, 90], 50)
assert(g.passed(), [70, 90])
[g.passed(), g.all_passed()]

description: A class-level rule calls a method that reads with leading dots
code:
class Rect(this.w, this.h):
    def area() => .w * .h
$Rect.big = .area() > 10
r = Rect(3, 4)
s = Rect(2, 2)
assert(r.big, true)
[r.big, s.big]

description: A declaration that calls a reading method follows the instance
code:
class Temp(this.c):
    def f() => .c * 9 / 5 + 32
t = Temp(100)
reading = t.f()
assert(reading, 212)
t.c = 0
reading

description: A subclass method reads the properties its parent declares
code:
class Shape(this.w, this.h)
class Prism(this.d) extends Shape:
    def volume() => .w * .h * .d
p = Prism(4)
p.w = 2
p.h = 3
assert(p.volume(), 24)
p.volume()
